mainTopic: Is כזית בכדי אכילת פרס דאורייתא? אביי challenges רב דימי from כותח and from 'שאני אומר' in mixtures of תרומה
overview: רב דימי had taught that permitted food joins forbidden food to reach the minimum amount only in the laws of a נזיר. אביי challenges this from a source that speaks of a כזית in a mixture. רב דימי answers that the source means a real כזית of the forbidden food eaten within the time of אכילת פרס, and he confirms that this measure is דאורייתא. אביי asks why, then, the רבנן disagree with רבי אלעזר about כותח הבבלי. רב דימי explains that with כותח you never actually eat a כזית of חמץ in that time. אביי then brings a ברייתא about two spice mortars and two pots, where we rely on 'שאני אומר' to permit both. רב דימי first shows that the question bothers every view. He then answers that תרומה of spices is only rabbinic. אביי brings a similar ברייתא about baskets of regular produce, and רב דימי's reply comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Isn't the Reason That Permitted Food Joins Forbidden Food?
steps.stepSummary: אביי finishes his challenge: the source he quoted must be counting permitted food together with forbidden food, which goes against רב דימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't it because the permitted food combines with the forbidden food?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי ends his attack. He says the source he just quoted only works if permitted food helps make up the minimum amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי had said that היתר מצטרף לאיסור only applies to a נזיר. If a source outside of נזיר also counts the permitted food toward the כזית, that would show the rule applies everywhere, and רב דימי's teaching would fall.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines, joins together to make up a minimum amount

phrases.english: Is it not because the permitted food
combines with the forbidden food?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge, which began before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that היתר מצטרף לאיסור applies only to נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A source outside נזיר seems to count permitted food toward a כזית, so the rule must apply elsewhere too.

steps.title: The כזית Means a כזית Eaten Within אכילת פרס
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that the כזית in the source is a real כזית of the forbidden food, eaten within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: No. What does 'a כזית' mean? That there is a כזית of the forbidden food within the time of eating a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי rejects אביי's reading. He says the source is not counting permitted food at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The mixture holds enough forbidden food that, while eating it, a person swallows a full כזית of the forbidden part within the time of אכילת פרס. The permitted food does not add to the amount. The forbidden food alone reaches the minimum, just spread out over a short time.

keyTerms.meaning: An olive-sized amount, the minimum amount for punishment
Within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea of כזית בכדי אכילת פרס as a different reason someone can be liable for eating a mixture. That reason has nothing to do with permitted food joining forbidden food.

phrases.english: He said to him: No,
what is meant by 'a כזית'?
That there is a כזית of the forbidden food
within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge by reading the source differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כזית in the source counts the permitted food too
steps.terutzMaskana: The כזית is all forbidden food, eaten within the time of אכילת פרס

steps.title: Is אכילת פרס From the Torah?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether the rule of eating a כזית within the time of אכילת פרס is a Torah-level law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the time of eating a half-loaf a Torah law?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks a clarifying question about רב דימי's answer: is this time measure really דאורייתא?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone gets Torah punishment for eating a mixed כזית within אכילת פרס, the measure must come from the Torah. אביי wants to confirm this before building his next challenge on it.

keyTerms.meaning: From the Torah, a Torah-level law
The time it takes to eat a half-loaf of bread

phrases.english: And the time of eating a half-loaf,
is it a Torah law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the basis of רב דימי's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is a Torah-level measure

steps.title: Yes, It Is From the Torah
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי confirms that אכילת פרס is דאורייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives a short answer: yes, it is a Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this, רב דימי commits to the position that eating a כזית of forbidden food within the time of אכילת פרס brings Torah punishment. אביי will now test that position.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes.

steps.title: Then Why Do the רבנן Disagree About כותח הבבלי?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges: if אכילת פרס is דאורייתא, the רבנן should agree with רבי אלעזר that eating כותח on פסח brings Torah punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do the רבנן disagree with רבי אלעזר about Babylonian כותח?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses רב דימי's 'yes' to attack. He points to a known argument about כותח הבבלי, a dip that has חמץ mixed in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that eating כותח on פסח brings punishment, and the רבנן say it does not. If a כזית within אכילת פרס brings Torah punishment, the רבנן should also say a person is punished when he eats enough כותח. Their disagreement suggests they do not accept this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Babylonian כותח, a sharp dip made with bread crumbs (חמץ)

phrases.english: If so, why
do the רבנן disagree with רבי אלעזר
phrases.notes: Some versions read רבי אליעזר here. Either way, it's the one who says you're punished for eating כותח on פסח.

phrases.english: about Babylonian כותח?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that אכילת פרס is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it were דאורייתא, the רבנן would have to make someone liable for eating כותח, yet they exempt him.

steps.title: With כותח, You Never Get a כזית in Time
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי answers that כותח is a special case. Eating it straight is too strange to count, and dipping in it never gives a כזית within אכילת פרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Leave Babylonian כותח aside, because there you can't get a כזית within the time of a half-loaf. If he swallows it straight, his way of eating is not counted, since no normal person eats like that. If he dips food into it, you won't find a כזית within the time of a half-loaf.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains that the argument about כותח does not touch the rule of אכילת פרס. In real life, a person eating כותח never reaches a כזית of חמץ in that time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are only two ways to eat כותח. Eating it straight is so unusual that the law ignores it. Dipping food into it uses only a little, too little to reach a כזית of חמץ in time. So the רבנן can accept אכילת פרס as דאורייתא and still exempt כותח.

keyTerms.meaning: His way of acting doesn't count, because everyone else acts differently

steps.whatToRemember: The argument about כותח is not about whether אכילת פרס is דאורייתא. It is about the fact that כותח never gives you a כזית of חמץ in that time.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב דימי is backing off from saying אכילת פרס is דאורייתא. He keeps that rule and only says כותח never meets its conditions.

phrases.english: He said to him: Leave aside Babylonian כותח,
because there is no כזית
within the time of eating a half-loaf.
If he swallows it straight,
phrases.notes: He means eating the sharp dip by itself like food, not as a dip.

phrases.english: his way of eating is cancelled by the way all people eat.
If he dips food into it,
you will not find a כזית
within the time of eating a half-loaf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב דימי against the כותח challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: the facts of כותח never meet the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן reject אכילת פרס as a Torah measure
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן accept it, but כותח never gives a כזית of חמץ within that time

steps.title: A New Challenge: Two Mortars and Two Pots
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a ברייתא: spices from a תרומה mortar and a חולין mortar fell into a תרומה pot and a חולין pot, and both pots are permitted. We assume each fell into its own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised an objection: Two spice mortars, one of תרומה and one of חולין, and in front of them two pots, one of תרומה and one of חולין. These fell into these. Both are permitted, because I say: the חולין fell into the חולין, and the תרומה fell into the תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי opens a new challenge to רב דימי by quoting a ברייתא. This step only sets up the source; the point of the attack comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We don't know which spices fell into which pot, yet the ברייתא is lenient. It assumes the חולין spices fell into the חולין pot and the תרומה spices fell into the תרומה pot. אביי will use this case to question רב דימי's position.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce given to a כהן, forbidden to non-כהנים
For I say: we assume the lenient possibility

phrases.english: He raised an objection: Two spice mortars,
one of תרומה
and one of חולין.
And in front of them were two pots,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין,
phrases.english: one of תרומה and one of חולין,
and these fell into those,
phrases.notes: The spices from the mortars fell into the pots, and nobody knows which went where.

phrases.english: both are permitted,
because I say:
the חולין fell into the חולין,
and the תרומה fell into the תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the כותח answer, אביי turns to a new source to challenge רב דימי
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim (Step 4) that כזית בכדי אכילת פרס is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא is set up here; Step 8 spells out how it challenges רב דימי.

steps.title: Why rely on 'שאני אומר' if אכילת פרס is Torah law?
steps.stepSummary: אביי spells out his challenge from the spice ברייתא. If a כזית within אכילת פרס is Torah law, we should worry that the תרומה spices fell into the חולין pot. So why are we lenient?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that a כזית eaten within the time of אכילת פרס is Torah law, why do we say 'because I say' (each fell into its own kind)?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes the challenge he started in Step 7. He explains exactly why the spice ברייתא is a problem for רב דימי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה spices fell into the חולין pot, a person eating from that pot could eat a כזית of תרומה within אכילת פרס. If that counts at Torah level, it is a Torah-level doubt, and we normally do not rely on a lenient guess like 'שאני אומר' in a Torah-level doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Because I say': a rule that lets us assume the lenient explanation of what happened
'If it would enter your mind': if you really thought so

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that eating a כזית within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf is Torah law,
why do we say 'because I say'?
phrases.notes: He means the line in the spice ברייתא from Step 7: the חולין spices fell into the חולין pot.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא, אַמַּאי אָמְרִינַן ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the objection whose source was quoted in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim (Step 4) that אכילת פרס is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being lenient with 'שאני אומר' only makes sense if the possible mixing is not a Torah-level problem. So אכילת פרס should not be Torah law.

steps.title: רב דימי shows the question bothers everyone
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי pushes back. Even if you reject אכילת פרס as Torah law, would you say the permitted food joins with the forbidden food? Then the same question remains: why say 'שאני אומר'?
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what would you say? That the permitted food combines with the forbidden food? Then why do we say 'because I say'?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers with a counter-question. He shows that אביי's question is not a special problem for his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If אכילת פרס is not the measure, the other option is that the permitted food joins with the forbidden food to make up the amount. Then the mixture would still be forbidden, and 'שאני אומר' is just as hard to explain. Since the question works against every view, it cannot disprove רב דימי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, what?' — so what is your alternative?
Permitted food joins with forbidden food to complete the needed amount

steps.confusionAlert: רב דימי is not agreeing that הֶיתֵּר מִצְטָרֵף לְאִיסּוּר. He uses it to show that אביי's question causes a problem for every view, so it is not a real attack on him.

phrases.english: Rather, what would you say?
That the permitted food combines with the forbidden food?
Then why do we say 'because I say'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns אביי's question around so it applies to everyone.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the spice ברייתא proves anything about אכילת פרס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The question is just as strong against the other approach, so it cannot decide between them.

steps.title: Spice תרומה is only rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי gives the real answer. תרומה from spices is only מדרבנן, so the רבנן could be lenient with 'שאני אומר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, leave aside the case of תרומה of spices, because it is only rabbinic.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי explains why the spice case does not disprove him. That kind of תרומה is only a rabbinic law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency of 'שאני אומר' fits a doubt about a rabbinic law. So the spice ברייתא tells us nothing about Torah-level measures like אכילת פרס.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Leave it aside': this case is no proof

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next move. אביי now has to find a case of Torah-level תרומה where the רבנן still use 'שאני אומר'.

phrases.english: Rather, leave aside the case of תרומה of spices,
since it is only rabbinic.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הַנַּח לִתְרוּמַת תַּבְלִין דְּרַבָּנַן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the real answer after the counter-question.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the source: the case is about rabbinic תרומה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The spice ברייתא shows the רבנן are lenient even where a Torah-level כזית might be eaten.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spice תרומה is only מדרבנן, so being lenient there proves nothing about Torah law.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: two baskets that spilled
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings another ברייתא. Two baskets, one of תרומה and one of חולין, spilled into two containers, one of חולין and one of תרומה. Both are permitted, because we assume each fell into its own kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: He objected: There were two baskets, one of תרומה and one of חולין. In front of them were two סאה containers, one of חולין and one of תרומה. These fell into those. Both are permitted, because I say: חולין fell into חולין, and תרומה fell into תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a new source to restart his challenge. This step quotes the case. The point of the attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is about regular produce, not spices, so it is not the spice תרומה that רב דימי just set aside as rabbinic. Even so, the ברייתא relies on 'שאני אומר' to permit both containers.

keyTerms.meaning: Containers holding a סְאָה (a measure of volume)

phrases.english: He raised an objection against him:
Two baskets,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין.
phrases.english: one of תרומה and one of חולין.
And in front of them were two סאה containers,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין וְאַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה,
phrases.english: one of חולין and one of תרומה,
and these fell into those —
phrases.notes: The baskets spilled into the containers, but we don't know which went into which.

phrases.english: both are permitted.
Because I say:
the חולין fell into the חולין,
and the תרומה fell into the תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ: שְׁתֵּי קוּפּוֹת, אַחַת שֶׁל תְּרוּמָה וְאַחַת שֶׁל חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the spice case was pushed aside, אביי brings a similar case that is not about spices.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that אכילת פרס is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Quotes a case of regular produce where the רבנן still rely on 'שאני אומר'.

steps.title: The same question about the baskets
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks again: if a כזית within אכילת פרס is forbidden by the Torah, why do we rely on 'שאני אומר' in the basket case?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think a כזית within the time of אכילת פרס is forbidden, why do we say 'because I say'?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his new challenge. He uses the same wording as before, now aimed at the basket ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תרומה basket fell into the חולין container, someone eating from it could eat a כזית of תרומה within אכילת פרס. If that is a Torah prohibition, it is hard to see why the ברייתא is lenient. The spice answer does not obviously cover this case, and רב דימי's reply comes on the next amud.
steps.whatToRemember: אביי keeps attacking with the same pattern: if the רבנן rely on 'שאני אומר', they must not treat אכילת פרס as Torah law. The spice case was pushed aside as rabbinic. Now the basket case needs an answer.

phrases.english: And if it would enter your mind
that a כזית eaten within the time it takes to eat a half-loaf is forbidden,
why do we say 'because I say'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ כְּזַיִת בִּכְדֵי אֲכִילַת פְּרָס אָסוּר, אַמַּאי אָמְרִינַן ״שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: States the point of the attack based on the ברייתא quoted in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי's claim that אכילת פרס is דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being lenient with 'שאני אומר' about this תרומה suggests that eating a כזית within אכילת פרס is not a Torah prohibition.
